protocol.request: Stable review UUID, saga UUID, independent reviewer UUID, expected revision and case reference; callers cannot select an asset outcome.
protocol.authorization: An explicit trusted review authorizer grants operator-policy evidence. Trade participants are rejected even if an adapter would authorize them.
protocol.observations: Fresh payment, delivery and compensation lookups use the unchanged complete operation identities under the same saga lock as automatic advance. No provider apply occurs during review.
protocol.uncertainResults: UNKNOWN, null, runtime/linkage failure, inconsistent combinations or contradiction of any prior APPLIED evidence remain MANUAL_REVIEW with a new audit entry.
protocol.persistence: Outer schema v2 stores the current schema-v1 saga and ordered review records in one atomic file. Ordinary create/replace retains schema v1 until a review occurs. Later automatic refunds retain audit history.
protocol.retry: Same review ID/request requires current operator authorization and returns the original record without querying again or rewriting evidence. Changed payloads, stale revisions and exhausted budgets reject.

failureMatrix: Completed delivery after expired trade permit is reconciled without refund or new transfer.
Paid-only reconciliation schedules the existing idempotent refund; real file failure after refund application preserves old bytes and recovers without another refund.
Already refunded and all-absent outcomes close without external side effects.
A rejected refund can re-enter review and later recover while preserving both decisions.
Null/throwing/unloaded provider lookup and conflicting prior APPLIED results stay quarantined.
Participant self-review, denied/revoked authorization, missing evidence, unknown saga, stale revision and reused review ID reject.
Legacy repositories without audit capabilities and ordinary replace cannot reopen MANUAL_REVIEW.
Real pre-commit file failure preserves v1 bytes; lost post-commit response returns the exact original audit on retry.
Concurrent reviewers permit one revision winner; automatic refund waits for the complete reconciliation lock scope.
Snapshot/observation/reviewer/revision/tick/ordering/schema tampering rejects without rewriting the file.
Sixteen-entry and 64 KiB limits preserve all existing evidence; large legal legacy fields can hit the byte limit first.
Unknown legacy review origins and lost provider capability reject before querying.
